title: Compiler observation record, version 0
description: The output form a component in compiler/ writes after it has looked. It carries where it looked (observationPoints), what it found there in the six-state vocabulary of interfaces.md section 3, who to blame as a (pass, IR unit) pair, what happened at the link and artefact layers, and one honest verdict. compiler/schema/emit-observation.mjs is the reference writer -- a pure function plus a CLI, gated so that it cannot emit a claim stronger than the evidence in front of it -- and compiler/schema/validate-observation.mjs is the validator every record it produces is checked against before anyone sees it. There is still no component in this repository that READS a record back and acts on it, so the deliverable is the form, an implementation that writes it, and a validator that refuses a dishonest one. Written against the keyword subset that compiler/driver/lib/jsonschema.mjs implements -- see validate-observation.mjs --capability, and see the semantic rules that file adds, because several of the invariants below cannot be said in draft-07 at all, let alone in that subset.

context.description: Everything a re-run cannot reproduce, and nothing else (interfaces.md section 5). Removed as a whole subtree before digesting, so adding a field here can never move a digest.

evidenceDigest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical bytes of this record with `context` and `evidenceDigest` removed as whole subtrees. Absent means the record has not been sealed.

policy.description: Which policy decided this run. The digest is here so a verdict can be re-read years later against the rules that produced it.

counts.description: The counting contract, inside the record rather than only on the runner's stdout. A record whose `checked` is 0 has not checked anything, and that is a fact a reader must be able to see without re-running.

skippedNames.description: Every skipped case by name. A count without names is not auditable.

observationPoints.description: Where this record looked. A point that was not reached stays in the array with reached=false and a reason -- deleting it would turn `we could not look` into `there was nothing to look at`.

properties.description: One entry per declared security property. Keys are property ids from compiler/schema/properties.json; `kind` is the policy's vocabulary.

ratio.description: interfaces.md section 5 rule 4: every number in a record is an integer, so a ratio is a pair and never a float.

relativePath.description: Relative to the fixture root. The leading-separator and drive-letter forms are refused here as well as by the recursive check in the validator, because a record that names one machine is not evidence about a build.

propertyState.description: interfaces.md section 3, entire. The last two exist because `we did not see it` and `it is not there` are different claims.

verdictState.description: The honest verdict. UNSUPPORTED and VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE are both `not clean`: the first says the configuration is outside the measured envelope, the second says a check inside the envelope did not finish. EVIDENCE_MISMATCH is the measurement disowning itself -- the control did not survive, or the record contradicts its own history -- and it is not a finding about the program.

exitCode.description: interfaces.md section 7, unchanged. 3 is never conflated with 0.

unobserved.description: Everything this run could not observe, by name. A non-empty list here forbids VERIFIED_CLEAN.

checkpoint.description: The five checkpoints of policy.schema.json properties[].observeAt, unchanged so that a policy and a record use one vocabulary.

stage.description: Which compilation stage the checkpoint was reached in. `lto-backend` is separate from `compile` because the same checkpoint kind is reached twice under -flto, in two different processes, and a record that merged them would attribute a link-time pass to the frontend.

unreachedReason.description: Required when reached is false, and it carries the tool's own words rather than a paraphrase.

target.description: The target triple this point was reached for. Recorded because a property observed to survive on one target has not been observed to survive on another.

effectCount.description: interfaces.md section 4. `oracle` is a const rather than an enum on purpose: there is no permitted way to record a count taken by searching for a symbol name, because a deleted call leaves its `declare` behind and a name search then blames the pass that swept the declaration away.

naiveSymbolMatches.description: Optional, and only ever alongside callSites: what a name search would have said. Recording the disagreement is useful; recording only this number is the bug the const above forbids.

attribution.description: A pair, never a pass alone. LLVM's pipeline nests module inside call graph inside function inside loop, so `the seventh pass` is not a position anyone can point at. null means not applicable, never not looked at.

lineage.description: The lineage root that groups a function with its clones. Keying a history by name alone splits one logical function in two and invents a reintroduction that never happened.

point.description: The id of an entry in observationPoints. Cross-reference, checked by the validator rather than by the schema.

controlObservation.description: interfaces.md section 4: every fixture carries a control whose effect cannot be removed, and it is required here rather than optional. A measurement whose control also fell to zero is a broken measurement, not a finding -- which is what EVIDENCE_MISMATCH is for.

history.description: The whole sequence, in order, to the end of the pipeline. Array order is significant and is never sorted.

historyComplete.description: False when the sequence was cut short -- a pass budget, a crash, a truncated log. A record may say so; it may not then also say VERIFIED_CLEAN.

fate.description: What became of the IR unit itself. A vanished unit is not a lost property; merging the two is how a checker starts lying.

layers.description: The three layers below the IR. Each carries `observed` first, because the interesting failure is a layer that was never looked at being read as a layer that was clean.

ltoMode.description: `unknown` is a real answer and is not `none`. A driver that cannot tell whether the link ran an LTO backend has not observed the passes that ran there.

backendObserved.description: Whether the pass pipeline inside the LTO backend was observed. False with ltoMode full or thin means a whole optimisation pipeline ran unwatched, and that forbids VERIFIED_CLEAN.

decidedBy.description: The structural field that decided it, never a tool's human-readable line.

finding.description: interfaces.md section 2, unchanged. The id pattern is the reserved namespace table made structural: a component cannot invent a seventh namespace by writing one.
